chapter: After high school: riverfront and tailoring
title: After high school: riverfront sack sewing and Xavier
summary: At fifteen he considered medical school or athletics, worked on the riverfront sewing sacks, and saved money to attend Xavier for nearly two years.

blocks.x: That was my next question. You probably sort of accelerated. Is that when you got out of high school, what were you going to do in life? Did you know, did you think about actually what am I going to do now?
When I got out of high school, I'm 15 years of age.
I think we're on it. All right. We're back with Tech Stevens. July 21st, 1995. Reel number three.
This is a Friday. It's a Friday.
It's a Friday. Okay. So, we ended on that question. You know, what realistically, when you graduated from high school, what were your options?

What did you want to do with your life? Well, I didn't have any outstanding dreams. I was thinking about going to medical school. I stayed out of school for about a year. My mother took sick and I went to work on the riverfront. And I started sewing. I started as a water boy. And then I started elevated Sidney White, who was the foreman at the time, gave me an opportunity to move up so from water boy to sack sewer. Wait, what was that?

What job was that? Well, sewing sacks. In other words, like the sugar would come in. Oh, okay. If a bag would break, you jump in the hole of the ship. And right away, you got a needle and brown thread, and you sew those sacks up real quick, and you break it. Oh, okay. So, that's what I started doing. And after I saved up enough money, and I went down Ramport Street there for a little while, and I started sewing clothes on the weekend when I wasn't working on the riverfront. That's where I met Louis Silver. And I got the first hundred dollars, and I just went back there and put it back there at Xavier. I stayed there about a year and a half, almost two years, then I volunteered and went to the service.
Okay. So, when you got out, so when you, I mean out of high school you were kind of directionless. Yeah, right.
I didn't have any direct directions. I was thinking about going to medical school.
I, you know, I thought... Was that a real option? I mean, you know...

Well, between going to medical school or probably becoming an athlete to play baseball or football or whatever, but I was kind of small to play football. I didn't put weight on until I came out of the service. See, but I still was a good football player. But then again, nobody was looking at black football and baseball players locally. Not 1937. Not at that particular time. Because as we got into the 70s, it took a little while for New Orleans to really, in the 60s rather, to decide to let colleges come in here with black football players to play in Tulane Stadium. Mm-hmm.
